head: 0c046b73841fc411af39b28bf1290c75c22460ee
headline: The README now has a short "Running locally" section explaining how to start the shop and run its tests. It's documentation only and safe to ship.
what_changed: Added a "Running locally" section to the README, the project's front-page instructions for developers.
It explains how to start the shop's server, which runs on port 3000 (the local web address it uses) unless a different port is set.
It explains how to run the automated tests.
It notes there is nothing to install apart from Node.js (the program that runs the shop's code).

The shop itself, customers and checkout are unaffected. The work was saved on its own branch (a separate copy of the code). It was not published or turned into a PR (a request to merge the change) because the project has no online copy set up yet.
questions_for_developer: Should the README also say which minimum version of Node.js is needed? The built-in test runner only exists in fairly recent versions.
Where should this repository live online (for example GitHub) so this branch can be published and opened as a pull request?
good_news: The instructions match the project. The start and test commands, the default port 3000 and the option to change the port were all checked against the code.
The change is limited to documentation and doesn't touch any code customers use.
